newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate falls back to 11.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate falls back to 11.7 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average lending rate fell back to 11.7 percent on Thursday from 13.5 percent due to bank borrowers' weaker kuna demand.
Money market settlements shrank to 26.8 million kuna ($4.4 million) from Wednesday's 47.4 million and only around 15 million were fresh loans.
But the rates remained relatively high at 11.0 percent for interbank call money to a maximum 18.0 percent for two-month funds.
Insurers rolled over old one-week loans at 9.0 percent.
The central bank calculated the kuna midrates for Friday's dealings firmer at 6.0525 versus 6.1073 against the dollar and at 3.5744 versus 3.5751 against the German mark.
